chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sukuni. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:

A riding animal has seven rights upon its owner: do not make it carry more than it can bear, do not make its back a sitting place for conversation, begin by feeding it when you dismount, do not brand its face, do not strike its face for it glorifies [Allah], offer it water when you pass by it, and do not strike it when it is startled, but strike it when it stumbles, for it sees what you do not see.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven rights of animals over their owners in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq enumerates seven rights that a riding animal has upon its owner, covering issues of overloading, rest, feeding, branding, striking, watering, and understanding the animal's perception of the unseen. This hadith reflects Islam's comprehensive ethical framework extending to animal welfare, teaching that animals are sentient beings deserving of compassion and proper treatment.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma`il b. Muslim al-Sukuni.  He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad said:

A riding animal has seven rights on its owner: (1) Do not make it carry more than it can handle, (2) do not make its back a sitting (loitering) place for conversation, (3) feed it when it disembarks, (4) do not brand its face, (5) do not strike its face, for it glorifies [Allah], (6) offer it water when it passes by it, (7) do not strike it when it is startled, for it sees what you do not.
